title: Reproducing Deal and Grove 1965: the linear-parabolic law and the constants our growth program takes from it

sample.paper: “(111) surface oriented, Czochralski pulled, with an initial dislocation count of less than 100 cm-2”

sample.ours: DOPING: p_type_boron_1.45e16 (recorded; no program reads it)

sample.paper: “circular slices 22 mm in diameter and mechanically polished to 200 μ thickness”; “placed flat on a quartz boat”
“no initial oxide could be detected by experimental techniques”; for dry oxygen the authors adopt xi = 230 Å as an initial condition standing for a fast first regime
sample.ours: the program starts every oxide at x_i = 23 nm (PARAMETER, STATUS sourced); the sample cannot carry it
sample.note: The 230 Å is a property of the law, not of the slice; for wet oxygen the paper's xi is zero and our program still starts at 23 nm.

sample.paper: not stated; figures show close pairs of points at one time
sample.ours: one sample per temperature and gas, its thickness read at each plotted time

history.paper: “circular slices 22 mm in diameter and mechanically polished to 200 μ thickness”
“Cleaning procedures prior to oxidation included both organic and inorganic rinses using ultrasonic agitation to insure noncontaminated surfaces.”
history.ours: CLEAN: not_stated; the vocabulary has no solvent-and-acid ultrasonic rinse
history.note: Chemicals and the delay before oxidation are not given.

history.item: Insertion into the tube at 1200 °C, time before counting starts
history.paper: not stated: “Silicon slices were placed flat on a quartz boat during oxidation.”
history.ours: RUN Push DURATION 1 TEMP 1200->1200 AMBIENT dry_O2
history.note: A step of 1 s that changes nothing; it is there so the time a slice spends in the gas before the clock starts can be searched (VARY).

history.item: Dry oxidation at 1200 °C, up to 25 h
history.paper: “purified dry oxygen (water content less than 5ppm)”; “Oxidation temperature was controlled to ±1°C over the range 700° to 1200°C.”
history.ours: RUN Oxidation DURATION 90000 TEMP 1200->1200 AMBIENT dry_O2
the history ends when the oxidation ends

history.paper: “Oxide thicknesses were determined using multiple-beam interferometric techniques. Accuracy … for oxides thicker than 0.20 μ was ±40 Å. For thinner oxides, the accuracy was ±25 Å.”
history.note: Whether each point is a separate slice or one slice measured and put back is not stated.
